fields.c8-input: draft kept apart from the screen

notes.P7.3: Airplane mode, force-quit, relaunch. After the same splash as online, the full Home screen appeared with the greeting, the to-do section and a past expense, plus a line saying: You appear to be offline.
notes.P12.1: After an offline cold start, the Inbox listed both chats with previews, and the self-chat opened with its history from 2025. Neither had been opened in this run of the app.
notes.P12.2: Offline, a test message sent in the self-chat appeared in the conversation at once, drawn dimmed. The other messages stayed at full brightness. The line You appear to be offline stayed under the composer.
notes.P12.3: With the test message still pending, the app was force-quit and reopened in airplane mode. The message was still in the self-chat, still dimmed, and the Inbox row for the chat showed it as the preview.
notes.P12.4: With the app on the Home tab and the self-chat closed, airplane mode was turned off for 25 seconds and then on again. On reopening the chat offline, the message was at full brightness and its time had changed from 9:41 PM to 9:42 PM. Older history that had been placeholders was also filled in.
notes.P4.2: See P7.3 for the offline launch and P12.2 for the accepted offline message.
notes.P3.1: Offline, stored screens opened and a sent message was accepted and drawn dimmed until the network returned.
notes.P8.2: An unsent draft typed in the self-chat composer was still there after switching to the device home screen and back, and after a force-quit and relaunch.
notes.P8.4: After a force-quit with a draft in the composer, the app reopened on its Home tab. The draft was in the composer when the chat was opened again.
notes.P4.3: Same run as P8.4: start screen, draft kept.
notes.P8.3: With the self-chat open, the process was ended the way the system does it, keeping saved state. The app cold-started on its Home tab, not in the chat. The wait was simulated, not real.
notes.P7.4: Home after a force-quit from a chat, and Home after a system-style process death from a chat. The next-day case was not waited for.
notes.P11.1: Offline, chats and their history were shown both while the app stayed alive and after a force-quit and relaunch.
notes.P9.1: A message sent online appeared as the preview on the chat's Inbox row on going back. A message sent offline did the same, while still pending.
notes.P13.2: After each return of the network, with the app untouched, the offline line disappeared, pending messages were sent, a pending deletion was applied and missing chat history filled in.
notes.P11.6: Offline, the self-chat opened from the Inbox with its full earlier history, far more than the one-line preview on the Inbox row.
notes.P7.1: Cold starts drew a first frame after 1.5 to 2.7 seconds, and that frame was a splash that stayed until about 12 seconds after launch on this emulator. A return to the running app took 1.7 seconds.
notes.P7.2: A splash with the logo stayed until the complete Home screen appeared. No placeholder frame was captured. The same happened in airplane mode, see P7.3.
notes.P8.7: With the app on the Inbox tab, a link to the About settings page was opened from outside. The app showed About. Back led to the Account tab, the parent of About, and not to the Inbox.
notes.P8.5: With the app closed, a link to the About settings page cold-started the app on that page.
notes.P8.6: Back from the page reached by link led to the Account tab inside the app, which is the page's parent.
notes.P32.1: A long press on a chat message opened the app's own action list, with Copy message and Copy link. No selection handles appeared. Other screens were not tried.
notes.P4.1: Device settings showed 3.7 MB user data and 1.4 MB cache at the start. After the run: 6.2 MB user data and 0.9 MB cache. The growth was in user data, not in the area the system counts as cache.
notes.P32.2: System text size raised from 1.0 to 1.5. Labels on the Account tab kept exactly the same pixel bounds. One screen was measured. Each change of text size also returned the app to its Home tab.
